messages.subject: Bart_par4 with two balloon colors
parts:
Hey everyone,

I have a question about the bart_par4 model, in case anyone has come across a similar issue. We're using the version of the BART performed during fMRI with two different color balloons (blue and red) as well as white control balloons. The rewards for the red and blue balloons are associated with slightly different probability distributions (1/8 and 1/12). The bart_par4 model was designed on the original (one-balloon) task. Has anyone else thought about how to run the model for the two-balloon task? 

So far, I ran the model with our data as is, as well as separating the blue and red balloons and running the model on each color separately. I've thought about modifying the model but wasn't sure if I should do something to account for the two different distributions since they are not completely independent. 

If anyone has thought about this or has any ideas, I would really appreciate it. Thank you!

messages.author: 78b6642bb15bbd88
messages.subject: Re: Bart_par4 with two balloon colors
parts:
Hello, 
I am also a newbie but can I drop some thoughts..

I suggest you should start with the research question you had before doing the fmri task
- because the computational model is the mathematical implementation of your hypothesis.

If your research question was to compare different parameters i.e. learning rate between balloons, I think fitting the two separate models according to the color is appropriate
- in this case I would pool the all the subjects data with red balloon together and you need to modify the code

In addition, was the probability distributions(1/8) was fixed? and told to the participants?
If so, I think you should fix the learning rate parameter, since the participants would not learn from the task. 

I hope my comments makes some sense

Best wishes, 
Minchul

messages.author: ffdb56a10dd8712e
messages.subject: Re: Bart_par4 with two balloon colors
parts:
Thank you so much for your response! 

Just to clarify, the task has two balloon colors - red and blue. So each participant completes a number of trials, where some trials consist of pumping a red balloon, and some consist of pumping a blue. Each participant performs the same task. The red balloon follows a 1/8 probability distribution, and the blue 1/12.

The question is not whether behavior differs between the two balloon colors on each task (although that is interesting in itself). The question is whether our two clinical groups perform differently on the task, i.e., whether they have different learning rates or risk-taking parameters. The problem is that we want to make sure those parameters are derived correctly from the model when it's applied to a task with this different structure.  Does that make it clearer? 

Thank you,
Zoe

messages.author: 78b6642bb15bbd88
messages.subject: Re: Bart_par4 with two balloon colors
parts:
Hello, 

In my opinion, if you were to use the hBayesDM model without modifying, 
I think you can fit model for each of the two clinical groups and for each balloons.
In this case presuming the hierarchical structure of 

Clinical diagnosis 
            |
participant 
      |
Red balloon learning rate

Another way to estimate one's own learning rate is to  pool the each balloon in to one participant (but need to modify the model)

Clinical diagnosis 
            |
participant 
      |
Learning rate
      |
Red balloon learning rate, Blue balloon learning rate

Best wishes, 
Minchul

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Bart_par4 with two balloon colors
parts:
Hi Zoe, 

Sorry for the long delay!

In short, you need to modify the original Stan code (https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/commons/stan_files/bart_ewmv.stan). 

Here (in the original EWMV model), it is assumed that "p_burst" is estimated for each balloon. You probably need to set different "p_burst" for each balloon but with the same parameters for each person. Let me know if this helps!

Best,
Young
